items.name: F1-replacement
items.text: - R2 is `import (value)`, with a space and a computed specifier: `value` is on the list, the reader reads only a string-literal specifier, and the `import(` token does not match a call with a space before the parenthesis.

items.name: F1-insertion
items.text: - R2's space also passes with a literal specifier, which the reader reads and admits: `export const value = () => import ('node:crypto');` (V9) and `import value = require ('node:crypto'); export { value };` (V7, which `tsc` emits through `createRequire` from `module`) each build and export the whole of `node:crypto`, `randomUUID` included, with every row green, "takes only createHash from node:crypto" among them (review R-GP-IMPL-SUPPORT-LEAF-GUARDS-2 F1). Without the space, the forbidden-token row kills each.

items.name: N1-residual
items.text: - **The createHash row reads module declarations only.** A local `export { createHash };` in `sha256.ts`, re-exported by `index.ts`, passes every row and builds: the leaf then exports the hash constructor itself (review R-GP-IMPL-SUPPORT-LEAF-GUARDS-2 N1, mutant V8). It reaches nothing but hashing.

items.name: N3-disclosure (repair-r2 item 5)
items.text: - **The no-write row reads assignment expressions only.** A destructuring write to an allowed global, `[Object.freeze] = [(value) => value];` (U4) or `({ value: Object.freeze } = { value: (bytes) => bytes });` (U5), passes every row (review R-GP-IMPL-SUPPORT-LEAF-GUARDS-2 N3). By the visitor's reading, so do a for-in or for-of target, `++`, `--` and `delete` [Inferred].
